title: Token-stride orchestrator: length-aware compaction & prefill-aware padding minimizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
We continue to see padding waste in multi-tenant serving where short and long sequences are coalesced into the same micro-batches. Existing bucketizers are static or histogram-only and do not account for prefill vs decode phase differences, kernel affinity, or per-request KV cache costs.

Goal:
Design and implement a Token-Stride Orchestrator (TSO) that dynamically forms micro-batches by: 1) sliding-window seqlen histograms, 2) compaction windows that allow short tokens to 'stride' into denser micro-batches, and 3) prefill-aware coalescence that treats prefill-heavy requests differently from purely decode work. The TSO should reduce padding tokens and net token compute cost while preserving or improving p95 latency SLO for decode requests.

Scope:
- Runtime change: batch formation stage (prefill and decode queues) + scheduler hints for kernel selection.
- No model architecture changes.
- Backwards-compatible config toggles and telemetry.

High-level approach:
1) Adaptive stride buckets: maintain an N-window histogram of incoming sequence lengths per serving shard. Buckets are adaptive with variable width; a stride parameter allows small sequences to be concatenated into one micro-batch slot if headroom exists, up to a configurable stride limit.
2) Phase-aware coalescer: track whether a request is prefill-dominant (long static prefix) or decode-dominant (short incremental tokens). Prefill-dominant requests are grouped to maximize KV-cache reuse and reduce duplicate prefix work. Decode-dominant requests are scheduled to favor low-latency paths.
3) Kernel hinting metadata: the orchestrator emits kernel-affinity hints (e.g., int8-quantized, fused-attn-friendly) along with micro-batch composition to the scheduler so that kernel selection can minimize memory fragmentation and kernel-switch overhead.
4) Graceful fallback: if SLO targets are threatened, the TSO falls back to latency-first packing (no extra compaction) for the affected shard.

Implementation details (engineering notes):
- Maintain per-shard sliding histogram with exponentially-weighted decay to adapt to traffic shifts.
- Compaction algorithm: greedily pack sequences into micro-batch slots with a scoring function: score = (saved_padding_tokens * kernel_efficiency_hint) - (expected_latency_penalty * risk_factor).
- Prefill coalescence: detect common prefix hashes within a 500ms window and tag requests to reuse prefix traces.
- Scheduler integration: add an opaque hint field to the dispatcher proto: kernel_hint and pack_ratio_target. Keep compatibility by treating hints as advisory.
- Telemetry: emit microbatch composition metrics (avg slot fill, padding_tokens_per_batch, prefill_coalesced_count) and SLO impact traces.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Increased packing may raise decode tail latency for some requests. Mitigation: conservative default stride=1.2 and automatic rollback when p95 increases >5%.
- Risk: Kernel fragmentation if different micro-batches require different innermost kernels. Mitigation: incorporate kernel affinity into pack score and prefer homogeneous micro-batches where possible.
- Risk: Prefill hashing costs. Mitigation: use 64-bit rolling hash and sample-based signature to limit CPU overhead.

Success metrics (baseline comparison on canary):
- Padding token reduction >= 28% across mixed workloads (chat + batch)
- End-to-end token compute cost reduction >= 12%
- p95 decode latency regression <= 5% (absolute), p99 unchanged or improved
- No customer-facing errors introduced during 2-week canary

Acceptance criteria:
- Deployed TSO toggled-on in canary pool with telemetry reporting.
- Telemetry confirms padding token reduction >= target across 7-day rolling window.
- No SLO violation alerts triggered during canary; if triggered, automated rollback succeeds.
- Unit and integration tests covering packing edge cases, prefill matching, and hint propagation exist and pass in CI.
- One end-to-end perf experiment comparing baseline vs TSO with reproducible benchmark notebook and instructions.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature toggle behind runtime flag; default OFF globally.
2) Internal canary: 5% traffic, dedicated shard group, 7-day stability window.
3) Expand to 25% if metrics good for 7 days.
4) 100% gradual ramp with automated checks and canary rollback on SLO breach.

Backward compatibility and ops controls:
- Config knobs: stride_limit, pack_score_threshold, prefill_window_ms, kernel_hint_mode (advisory/required/disabled), rollback_on_p95_pct.
- Console dashboard: microbatch composition, per-shard padding reduction, and rollback triggers.
- Emergency killswitch via console and API.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: compaction scoring, stride limit enforcement, histogram decay behavior.
- Integration: end-to-end in staging with synthetic mixed-length workload (chat + large prefill).
- Perf bench: replicate production-like arrival distributions and measure token compute, p95/p99 latencies.
- Safety test: inject sudden surge of long-prefill requests and validate fallback behavior.

Operational runbooks (short):
- If p95 increases beyond threshold, toggle kernel_hint_mode to disabled then disable TSO.
- If error rate increases, capture microbatch composition for last 10 minutes and open ENG-incident with trace.

Estimated effort and milestones:
- 2w: prototype compaction algorithm and unit tests (local).
- 3w: integrate with dispatcher hints and basic telemetry.
- 2w: staging perf + iteration.
- 1w: canary rollout and monitoring dashboard.

Notes on differences from existing bucketizers:
- Existing systems use static bucket boundaries or histogram snapshots. TSO introduces a stride-based compaction with phase-awareness and kernel affinity hints, enabling better trade-offs between padding reduction and kernel fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: TSO enabled in canary with telemetry
Padding tokens >=28% reduction over baseline across mixed workloads
Unit and integration tests present and passing
Benchmark notebook and results checked into repo
tradeoffs_decisions: Default stride conservative (1.2) to reduce tail regressions
Kernel hints are advisory by default to avoid hard failures
Prefill coalescence limited to 500ms window to keep CPU low
